name: Paldiski
title: Paldiski Ro-Ro and Car Carrier Hull Gauging | UTM Estonia
description: Thickness measurement in Paldiski at the South and North harbours: UTM of ro-ro, ro-pax and car carrier decks, ramps and tanks, plus bulk and tanker gauging.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Paldiski, West of Tallinn
intro: Paldiski, on the Pakri peninsula west of Tallinn, has two cargo harbours side by side: the Port of Tallinn's South Harbour, busy with ro-ro, new cars and bulk, and the privately owned North Harbour. A ro-pax service links the town with Kapellskär in Sweden, and the bay tends to stay more open in winter than the harbours further east. Vehicle decks, ramps and tanks are the usual gauging scope. Our technicians are sent from India to the ship for each job, with nothing kept at the port between visits.

highlights.p: The South Harbour has large car terminals and ro-ro berths with links to ports around the Baltic and the North Sea. Vehicle carriers and ro-ro ships berth for hours rather than days, which suits staged gauging of decks, ramps and tanks.

DFDS runs a ro-pax service between Paldiski and Kapellskär on the Swedish side, carrying freight and drivers. Her lay-overs and her docking are the windows for measuring vehicle decks, voids and ramp structure without losing sailings.

highlights.h: Open water for more of the winter
highlights.p: The Pakri peninsula reaches out into the open Gulf of Finland, and Paldiski Bay generally stays clearer of ice than the sheltered bays further east. Winter calls are more predictable as a result, though ice restrictions can still apply in a hard winter.

port.h: Paldiski's two harbours and the ships they handle
p: Paldiski lies some 45 kilometres west of Tallinn on the Pakri peninsula, near the north-west corner of mainland Estonia. Its harbour has been valued for centuries because the bay is deep and opens straight onto the Gulf of Finland, and in the Soviet period the town was a closed military base. Today there are two cargo harbours next to each other. The South Harbour, owned by the Port of Tallinn, is the larger, with berths for ro-ro, general and break-bulk cargo, dry bulk and liquid bulk, extensive car terminals and an industrial park behind the quays. The North Harbour is privately owned and run, with a smaller number of berths handling cargo of its own.

Ro-ro is the core trade. Ro-ro and con-ro ships connect Paldiski with ports in Finland, Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and the United Kingdom, carrying trailers, rolling stock and Estonian import and export cargo, while vehicle carriers bring new cars to the South Harbour's car terminals for distribution across the region. DFDS's ro-pax crosses to Kapellskär, north of Stockholm, with freight and drivers. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships work at the bulk and break-bulk berths, tankers use the liquid berths, and the Port of Tallinn has invested in a new deep-water quay at the South Harbour intended for offshore wind components and military mobility cargo, with land behind it for storing and preparing large components.

Port stays at Paldiski are short to medium. Ro-ro and vehicle carriers work their cargo in hours, the ro-pax keeps a timetable, and bulk and tanker calls run over a day or so, which is the rhythm a gauging plan has to follow. Winter is gentler here than in the inner Gulf of Finland: the bay generally stays more open than Tallinn Bay or Muuga Bay, although in a severe winter drift ice reaches the coast and the Estonian authorities can impose ice-class restrictions. Paldiski's other recent addition is the LNG quay at Pakrineeme, built in 2022 during the gas supply crisis so that a floating import terminal could berth there if needed. For a superintendent, Paldiski is a ro-ro port with some bulk and liquid trade, where the ship's own schedule sets the pace.

facilities.h: Gauging at the South Harbour, North Harbour and car terminals
p: On ro-ro and vehicle carriers the work happens while the cargo flows. Once a deck has been discharged and before it loads again, the team can measure deck plating, internal ramps and their hinges, the supports of hoistable decks where they can be reached, and the ballast and void spaces below. Vehicle carriers have many light decks, so the readings concentrate on the main and freeboard decks, the stern ramp and its foundations, and the lower decks, where condensation and road salt dripping from vehicles in winter drive corrosion. The ro-pax on the Kapellskär service is measured on lay-overs agreed with the operator, a section at a time.

Bulk carriers and general cargo ships at the South Harbour are gauged hold by hold during cargo operations, and tankers at the liquid berths under the terminal's and the ship's permit systems, with cargo tanks left for a gas-free period. We do not plan dockings at Paldiski, but Tallinn Shipyard at Kopli lies along the coast to the east, so a ship gauged at Paldiski can be docked in Tallinn with the same team following her there. Ships anchored off Paldiski before berthing can be reached by launch through the agent when the weather allows.
list: Paldiski South Harbour ro-ro berths — ro-ro and con-ro ships on North Sea and Baltic routes; deck, ramp and tank gauging between discharge and loading
South Harbour car terminals — vehicle carriers delivering new cars; main deck, stern ramp and lower-deck corrosion measurements during the call
Ro-pax berth for the Kapellskär service — vehicle deck, void and ramp structure gauging on lay-overs
South Harbour bulk and liquid berths — bulk carriers and tankers; hold gauging and deck and piping measurements during cargo operations

context.h: Estonian inspection, Baltic trade and defence cargo
p: Port state control at Paldiski is carried out by the Estonian Transport Administration under the Paris MoU. On ro-ro and ro-pax ships, inspectors look closely at shell doors, ramps and watertight integrity, and a ship whose stern ramp hinges or deck structure show wastage or cracking is likely to draw a deficiency. Many of the ro-ro services calling at Paldiski run entirely between EU ports, so their voyages fall wholly under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, and operators on those routes tend to plan steel work for the docking rather than lose sailings to unplanned repairs, which puts a premium on accurate gauging beforehand.

Paldiski has also become part of the logistics of the Baltic's eastern flank: the new South Harbour quay was co-financed through the EU's military mobility programme, and ro-ro ships carrying military vehicles and equipment call here. Charters for that kind of cargo can be fixed at short notice, and charterers often want recent evidence of a ship's condition, which can bring on-hire gauging with little warning. In winter, the Estonian ice-class restrictions for Paldiski are usually less demanding than those further east, but ro-ro ships on Gulf of Finland routes mostly hold Finnish-Swedish ice classes and carry the ice-belt wear that goes with them.

jobs.p: Most Paldiski jobs are ro-ro work: staged deck and ramp gauging on ships that are never in port for long, with crack detection on the hinges and lugs that carry ramp loads. The ro-pax brings planned docking preparation. Bulk and tanker calls bring conventional hold, deck and piping scopes, and on-hire or condition gauging appears when ro-ro ships are chartered for project or military cargo. Because Tallinn Shipyard is close, pre-docking gauging at Paldiski followed by in-dock verification at Kopli is a practical combination that one mobilisation can cover. Each visit is planned with the ship's officers so a complete deck or tank group is closed off before she sails.
list: Staged main-deck, ramp and ballast-tank gauging on a ro-ro ship over two Paldiski calls, ahead of her renewal survey
Magnetic particle crack detection on stern-ramp hinge lugs and locking devices of a vehicle carrier at the car terminal
Vehicle deck and void gauging on the Kapellskär ro-pax during lay-overs, building the record before her docking
On-hire condition gauging on a ro-ro ship chartered for military or project cargo, finished within her loading window
Hold and ballast-tank measurements on a general cargo ship at the South Harbour's break-bulk berths

logistics: The team flies into Tallinn Airport and continues by road west along the coast to Paldiski. Estonia is part of the Schengen area, so our technicians travel from India on Schengen visas, applied for as soon as the ship's call date is known. ISPS access to the South Harbour is arranged by the ship's agent with the Port of Tallinn, and access to the North Harbour with its operator. Where the ship is going on to dock at Kopli, the agent and the shipyard arrange the yard pass for the follow-on visit.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a vehicle carrier during a short Paldiski call?
faqs.a: A defined part of the scope, yes. Once a deck is clear of cars and before loading starts, we measure deck plating, ramps and the structure below that the crew can open. Car carriers rarely stay long, so we split a larger scope over several calls and agree with the chief officer which decks and tanks will be free at each visit. Ramp hinges and locking devices can be crack-tested in the same window.

faqs.q: What do you check on stern ramps and ramp hinges?
faqs.a: We gauge ramp plating, the ramp's stiffeners and the deck structure around its foundations, and use magnetic particle or dye penetrant testing on hinge lugs, pin housings and the welds that carry ramp loads. Ramps on ro-ro ships calling at Paldiski cycle many times a week, so fatigue cracking is a real risk. The results go to the ship and to the class surveyor, who decides on repairs.

faqs.q: Is ice a concern for ships calling at Paldiski?
faqs.a: Less than at most Gulf of Finland ports. Paldiski Bay opens onto the open sea and generally stays clearer than the inner bays, so winter calls are more predictable. In a hard winter drift ice can still reach the coast and the Estonian authorities may set ice-class restrictions. Inside the ship, cold weather changes little except ventilation times and the couplant we use.

faqs.q: Can a ship gauged at Paldiski be docked in Tallinn with the same team?
faqs.a: Yes. Tallinn Shipyard at Kopli is along the coast to the east, so a ship gauged during a Paldiski call can go there for her docking and the same technicians can follow her, verifying bottom and shell readings and finishing the scope as staging and gas-freeing allow. The superintendent then has one continuous record rather than two separate reports.
